newsitem.title: USA: Flextech buys some TI semi units.
newsitem.headline: Flextech buys some TI semi units.

text.p: Singapore's Flextech Holdings Ltd said Thursday it had acquired several of Texas Instruments Inc's semiconductor equipment businesses.
The deal is worth $9.4 million, with $4.2 million payable at closing and the rest due over the next three years.
The businesses handles the design, manufacture and sales of inspection and conditioning equipment, laser marking equipment and vision OEM equipment for semiconductor assembly manufacturing.

"This transaction represents an excellent opportunity to integrate our core competencies into the manufacture of vision inspection and laser marking equipment used in the semiconductor industry," Flextech chief executive Joseph Au said in a company statement.
Flextech said the new business will be its first wholly owned U.S. operation and will be called Semiconductor Technologies & Instruments Inc.

It said the deal should close by the end of June and that about 50 employees will transfer to Flextech after it creates a U.S.-based infrastructure, which it said should be completed in less than 60 days.
